Let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be conjugate exponents. If $X$ and $Y$ are real random
variables in the spaces named by the corresponding clause of
[[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], then
$$\mathbb E[|XY|]\le\|X\|_p\|Y\|_q.$$

In particular, $XY$ is integrable.

derivations.claim: By [A1], all $X_{N,i}$ have the same distribution and every distinct pair has the same covariance. By [A3] and [F1], $\mathbb E X_{N,1}\to\mathbb E U$; the same $L^2$ convergence and $\mathbb E U^2<\infty$ give $\sup_N\|X_{N,1}\|_2<\infty$.

Write $X_i=X_{N,i}$ and $U_i=U_{N,i}$. The identity $X_1X_2-U_1U_2=(X_1-U_1)X_2+U_1(X_2-U_2)$ and [F1] give $|\operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_2)-\operatorname{Cov}(U_1,U_2)|\le \|X_1-U_1\|_2\|X_2\|_2+\|U_1\|_2\|X_2-U_2\|_2+|\mathbb EX_1\mathbb EX_2-\mathbb EU_1\mathbb EU_2|.$ By exchangeability the two $L^2$ differences have the same norm and both means converge as in step 1.1. Thus [A2]–[A3] imply $\operatorname{Cov}(X_{N,1},X_{N,2})\to0$.

Expanding the variance and using [A1] yields $\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_N)=N^{-1}\operatorname{Var}(X_{N,1})+(1-N^{-1})\operatorname{Cov}(X_{N,1},X_{N,2})\longrightarrow0,$ because the first variance is uniformly bounded by step 1.1 and the second term tends to zero by step 2.1. Also $\mathbb E\bar X_N=\mathbb E X_{N,1}\to\mathbb E U$ by step 1.1. Hence $\mathbb E|\bar X_N-\mathbb E U|^2=\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_N)+|\mathbb E\bar X_N-\mathbb E U|^2\to0$.

For each integer $N\ge2$, let $(X_{N,i},U_{N,i})_{i=1}^N$ be a jointly exchangeable row of real random pairs: its law is invariant when the same permutation is applied to every index. Assume that $U_{N,1},\ldots,U_{N,N}$ are pairwise uncorrelated, all have the law of a fixed square-integrable random variable $U$, and
$$\|X_{N,1}-U_{N,1}\|_2:=\bigl(\mathbb E|X_{N,1}-U_{N,1}|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $\operatorname{Cov}(V,W):=\mathbb E[(V-\mathbb EV)(W-\mathbb EW)]$. Then the empirical mean $\bar X_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N X_{N,i}$ converges to $\mathbb E U$ in $L^2$, meaning $\mathbb E|\bar X_N-\mathbb E U|^2\to0$, and hence in probability.

Let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be conjugate exponents. If $X$ and $Y$ are real random
variables in the spaces named by the corresponding clause of
[[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], then
$$\mathbb E[|XY|]\le\|X\|_p\|Y\|_q.$$

In particular, $XY$ is integrable.

derivations.claim: Holder's inequality [F2] on a probability space gives $\|X_{N,1}-U_{N,1}\|_2\le\|X_{N,1}-U_{N,1}\|_4$. Apply [F1] to each coordinate to obtain $\bar X_N\to\mathbb EU$ in probability.

Fix coordinates $r,s\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and set $V_{N,i}=X_{N,i,r}X_{N,i,s}$ and $W_{N,i}=U_{N,i,r}U_{N,i,s}$. The rows $(V_{N,i},W_{N,i})$ are jointly exchangeable. By Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|V_{N,1}-W_{N,1}\|_2\le\|X_{N,1,r}-U_{N,1,r}\|_4\|X_{N,1,s}\|_4+\|U_{N,1,r}\|_4\|X_{N,1,s}-U_{N,1,s}\|_4\to0.$ The product bounds follow from [F2]; the factors tending to zero follow from [A2], and the remaining fourth moments are bounded by [A2]. Since the $W_{N,i}$ are iid and square-integrable, they are pairwise uncorrelated. Thus [F1] applied to these scalar rows gives $N^{-1}\sum_iX_{N,i,r}X_{N,i,s}\to\mathbb E[U_rU_s]$ in probability.

Entrywise, $C_N=N^{-1}\sum_iX_{N,i}X_{N,i}^T-\bar X_N\bar X_N^T$. The first term converges to $\mathbb E[UU^T]$ by step 2.1 and the second to $(\mathbb EU)(\mathbb EU)^T$ by step 1.1. Their difference is $\operatorname{Cov}(U)$, proving the claim.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$. Let
the state dimension at time
$t$ be a positive integer $d_t$ for $0\le t\le T$, and the observation
dimension at time $t$ be a positive integer $p_t$ for $1\le t\le T$.
Choose deterministic matrices
$F_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_{t-1}}$ and
$H_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t\times d_t}$, a mean $m_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$, and
symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices, meaning $v^TPv\ge0$ for every
real vector $v$ of matching dimension,
$P_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times d_0}$,
$Q_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_t}$, and
$R_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t\times p_t}$. A **linear-Gaussian state-space model
with independent noises** is the general finite-horizon kernel model
([[def-general-state-space-model-by-kernels]]) with initial law
$\mu_0=N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$ and transition and observation kernels
$$K_t(x,\cdot)=N_{d_t}(F_t x,Q_t),\qquad G_t(x,\cdot)=N_{p_t}(H_t x,R_t).$$
All Gaussian laws use the convention of
[[def-multivariate-normal-law]], which allows singular covariance matrices.

Its independent-noise representation consists of random vectors
$x_0,q_1,r_1,\ldots,q_T,r_T$ on a common probability space, with
$x_0\sim N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$, $q_t\sim N_{d_t}(0,Q_t)$,
$r_t\sim N_{p_t}(0,R_t)$, all mutually independent in the sense of
[[def-independent-random-elements]] (their generated sigma-algebras are
independent), and equations
$$x_t=F_t x_{t-1}+q_t,\qquad y_t=H_t x_t+r_t\qquad(1\le t\le T).$$
The local path-law theorem proves that every allowed parameter tuple has
such a finite representation, that its induced kernels are the displayed
$K_t,G_t$, and that its path law is the general kernel-product law.

This definition imposes the stated noise law and independence assumptions;
it does not establish their empirical adequacy. It supplies no filtering
algorithm, posterior recursion, or convergence claim. Any separate formula
that inverts an observed innovation covariance must assume that covariance is
positive definite at the point of inversion.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $m\ge1$ be finite, let $d_j\ge1$, and let
$Z_j$ for $1\le j\le m$ be mutually independent random elements of
$\mathbb R^{d_j}$. Suppose $Z_j\sim N_{d_j}(a_j,\Sigma_j)$, where each
$\Sigma_j$ is symmetric positive semidefinite. Put
$D=\sum_{j=1}^m d_j$, $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)$,
$a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$, and
$\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_m)$. Then
$$Z\sim N_D(a,\Sigma).$$
No covariance block needs to be invertible.

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_0,\ldots,d_T$,
and positive observation dimensions $p_1,\ldots,p_T$. The input is a
linear-Gaussian model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]], with
matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_{k-1}}$ and
$H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, initial mean $m_0$, and symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariances $P_0,Q_k,R_k$. Its state and observation
equations are
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k,$$
where $q_k\sim N(0,Q_k)$ and $r_k\sim N(0,R_k)$ are centered and mutually
independent across all times and of $X_0$.

The admissible data are vectors $y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$ for which every
innovation covariance encountered below is positive definite. Positive
definite means $u^TS_ku>0$ for every nonzero $u\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$. The
algorithm returns predicted and updated means and covariances and the
innovation and gain at each time. Initialize
$$m_{0|0}=m_0,\qquad P_{0|0}=P_0.$$
For $k=1,\ldots,T$, perform:

1. Predict:
$$m_{k|k-1}=F_km_{k-1|k-1},\qquad P_{k|k-1}=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k.$$
2. Form the innovation and its covariance:
$$v_k=y_k-H_km_{k|k-1},\qquad S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k.$$
3. Factor $S_k=L_kL_k^T$ with lower-triangular $L_k$ having positive
diagonal, using
[[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]].
Solve $L_kU_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}$ and $L_k^TK_k^T=U_k$ by triangular solves. This
defines $K_k^T=S_k^{-1}H_kP_{k|k-1}$, hence
$K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS_k^{-1}$, without explicitly forming $S_k^{-1}$.
4. Update:
$$m_{k|k}=m_{k|k-1}+K_kv_k,\qquad P_{k|k}=P_{k|k-1}-K_kS_kK_k^T.$$

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the returned pair is $(m_0,P_0)$. No
inverse of $P_0$, $Q_k$, or $R_k$ is used. This item defines the procedure
and makes no complexity, rounding-error, or numerical-stability claim.

Assume AC. Fix a finite-horizon model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]] with
state and observation equations
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k\qquad (1\le k\le T),$$
where $X_0\sim N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$, the centered Gaussian noises $q_k,r_k$ are
mutually independent across times and from $X_0$, and $P_0,Q_k,R_k$ are
symmetric positive semidefinite. Let the parameters and observations be
admissible for [[alg-kalman-filter]], so the recursively formed innovation
covariances
$$S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k$$
are positive definite for every $1\le k\le T$. Run that algorithm from
$m_{0|0}=m_0$ and $P_{0|0}=P_0$. Then, for each $0\le k\le T$, the map
$$\pi_k(y_{1:k},\cdot)=N_{d_k}(m_{k|k}(y_{1:k}),P_{k|k})$$
is an everywhere-defined filtering kernel for $X_k$ given $Y_{1:k}$ in the
sense of [[def-state-space-filtering-laws]]. The empty history at $k=0$ is a
singleton, and $\pi_0=N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$. In particular, these recursions
give an exact Gaussian conditional-law version at every observation history;
each $P_{k|k}$ is positive semidefinite. Singular initial, process,
measurement, predicted-state, and filtered-state covariances are allowed.
Equivalently, the covariance update can be written in Joseph form
$$P_{k|k}=(I-K_kH_k)P_{k|k-1}(I-K_kH_k)^T+K_kR_kK_k^T.$$
Only the innovation matrices being solved must be positive definite. No
pointwise uniqueness of a conditional-law version on null histories,
observation-density assumption, or numerical-stability claim is made.

Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. For $m\in\mathbb R^d$ and a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, a Borel probability law is denoted $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ when a vector X with that law satisfies $u\cdot X\sim N(u\cdot m,u^T\Sigma u)$ for every $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Such a law exists, has mean m and covariance Sigma, and can be realized as $m+\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ with independent standard-normal coordinates. Singular Sigma is allowed. Uniqueness will be proved in the following characteristic-function lemma.

derivations.claim: At $k=0$, the analysis members are iid with law $N(m_0,P_0)$ by their initialization, so the claim holds at the base time.

Assume the induction hypothesis: the members at time $k-1$ are iid with law $N(m_{k-1|k-1},P_{k-1|k-1})$. Each forecast is an affine image of the independent Gaussian pair $(U_{N,i}^{a,k-1},q_{N,i}^k)$. By [F2] the pair is jointly Gaussian; every scalar projection of its affine image is a scalar Gaussian projection, so [F5] makes the forecasts iid Gaussian with mean $m^f=F_km_{k-1|k-1}$ and covariance $P^f=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k$.

Since $P^f\succeq0$ and $R_k\succ0$, $S=H_kP^fH_k^T+R_k\succ0$, so $K=P^fH_k^TS^{-1}$ is defined. The independent Gaussian pair $(U_{N,i}^{f,k},y_k+\eta_{N,i}^k)$ and [F2] show that $U_{N,i}^{a,k}=A U_{N,i}^{f,k}+K(y_k+\eta_{N,i}^k)$, with $A=I-KH_k$, is Gaussian. Its mean is $m^f+K(y_k-H_km^f)$ and its covariance is $AP^fA^T+KR_kK^T=P^f-KSK^T,$ because $KS K^T=P^fH_k^TK^T=KH_kP^f$. These are precisely the Kalman update parameters in [F3].

For distinct member indices the pairs of forecast and perturbed observation are independent by the input independence and the induction hypothesis; applying the same deterministic affine update separately to each pair preserves independence. Therefore the updated members are iid with the Gaussian law from step 3.1. By [A1] and [F4] that law is the exact filtering law at the fixed data.

The initialization in step 1.1 is the base case, and step 4.1 proves the claim at time $k$ from the induction hypothesis at time $k-1$. Induction therefore gives the asserted iid exact filtering law for every $k\le T$.

Fix an ensemble size $N\ge2$, forecast map $\Psi$, observation map $G$, datum $y\in\mathbb R^p$, and observation covariance $\Gamma\succ0$. The input is a state ensemble $x^1,\ldots,x^N\in\mathbb R^d$, forecast-error draws $\xi^i$ that are independent across members and of the input ensemble, each with the caller-specified additive model-error law, and observation perturbations $\eta^i\sim N_p(0,\Gamma)$ under [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]. The observation perturbations are independent across members and independent of the forecast ensemble and forecast-error draws.

1. Forecast each member: $\widehat x^i=\Psi(x^i)+\xi^i$.

2. Form predicted observations $z^i=G(\widehat x^i)$, means $\bar x=N^{-1}\sum_i\widehat x^i$, $\bar z=N^{-1}\sum_i z^i$, and empirical covariance blocks
$$C_{xz}=N^{-1}\sum_i(\widehat x^i-\bar x)(z^i-\bar z)^T,\qquad C_{zz}=N^{-1}\sum_i(z^i-\bar z)(z^i-\bar z)^T.$$
The divisor-$N$ convention is part of this algorithm.

3. Form $S_N=C_{zz}+\Gamma$. Since $C_{zz}$ is positive semidefinite and $\Gamma$ is positive definite, $S_N$ is positive definite. Factor it by Cholesky and solve $S_NK_N^T=C_{xz}^T$ by triangular solves.

4. Update every member using its perturbed datum:
$$x^{a,i}=\widehat x^i+K_N(y+\eta^i-z^i).$$

Return the updated ensemble and its empirical mean and covariance. When $G(x)=Hx$, $C_{xz}=C_xH^T$ and $C_{zz}=HC_xH^T$, giving the usual sample-covariance Kalman gain. This item specifies the perturbed-observation variant; deterministic square-root updates are different finite-ensemble procedures. Finite ensembles in nonlinear models are approximations and carry no general posterior-exactness claim.

derivations.claim: Fix a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Applying it to the input states and errors permutes the forecast states and predicted observations by the same $\sigma$. Their empirical means are unchanged, while the sums defining $C_{xz}$ and $C_{zz}$ are unchanged because they only reorder their summands. Therefore $S_N$ and the common gain $K_N$ are unchanged.

With the same $K_N$, the update at permuted index $i$ is exactly the original updated state at index $\sigma(i)$, since its datum perturbation and reference variable are permuted along with that member. Thus the full updated tuple under $\sigma$ is a permutation of the original updated tuple. Its law is unchanged by [A1], which is joint exchangeability.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

2. Form predicted observations $z^i=G(\widehat x^i)$, means $\bar x=N^{-1}\sum_i\widehat x^i$, $\bar z=N^{-1}\sum_i z^i$, and empirical covariance blocks

3. Form $S_N=C_{zz}+\Gamma$. Since $C_{zz}$ is positive semidefinite and $\Gamma$ is positive definite, $S_N$ is positive definite. Factor it by Cholesky and solve $S_NK_N^T=C_{xz}^T$ by triangular solves.

Return the updated ensemble and its empirical mean and covariance. When $G(x)=Hx$, $C_{xz}=C_xH^T$ and $C_{zz}=HC_xH^T$, giving the usual sample-covariance Kalman gain. Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. For $m\in\mathbb R^d$ and a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, a Borel probability law is denoted $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ when a vector X with that law satisfies $u\cdot X\sim N(u\cdot m,u^T\Sigma u)$ for every $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Such a law exists, has mean m and covariance Sigma, and can be realized as $m+\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ with independent standard-normal coordinates. Singular Sigma is allowed. Uniqueness will be proved in the following characteristic-function lemma.

Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space and let $T:V\to V$ be
self-adjoint. Then $V$ has an orthonormal basis consisting of eigenvectors of
$T$.

Let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be conjugate exponents. If $X$ and $Y$ are real random
variables in the spaces named by the corresponding clause of
[[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]], then
$$\mathbb E[|XY|]\le\|X\|_p\|Y\|_q.$$

In particular, $XY$ is integrable.

derivations.claim: By [A1] and [F2]–[F3], each Gaussian vector is an affine image of finitely many standard normals. For every finite $p$, the integral of $|x|^p e^{-x^2/2}$ is finite because for sufficiently large $|x|$, $|x|^p\le e^{x^2/4}$ and $e^{-x^2/4}$ is integrable; bounded intervals contribute a finite integral. Finite-dimensional triangle inequalities then give finite moments for each vector input, with laws independent of $N$ and $i$. This proves the asserted state bound at $k=0$.

Assume the induction hypothesis that at time $k-1$ the state moments are bounded uniformly in $N,i$ at every finite order. The forecast formula in [F1] is a fixed linear map plus a Gaussian process-error draw. The triangle inequality and $ (a+b)^p\le2^{p-1}(a^p+b^p)$ for $a,b\ge0$ therefore give uniform bounds at every order for the forecast members $X_{N,i}^{f,k}$.

Write the forecast sample covariance as $C_N=N^{-1}\sum_iX_iX_i^T-\bar X\bar X^T$. Since $\|xx^T\|_{\rm op}=\|x\|^2$, Jensen's inequality for finite averages bounds the $p$th moment of the first term by $N^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E\|X_i\|^{2p}$ and bounds $\mathbb E\|\bar X\|^{2p}$ by the same average. Thus [F1] and the forecast bounds in step 2.1 give $\sup_N\mathbb E\|C_N\|_{\rm op}^p<\infty$ for every finite $p$.

The matrix $H_kC_NH_k^T$ is positive semidefinite, so $S_N=H_kC_NH_k^T+R_k$ has quadratic form at least that of $R_k$. Let $r_k>0$ be the least eigenvalue of $R_k$, which exists by [F4]. Every eigenvalue of $S_N$ is at least $r_k$, hence $\|S_N^{-1}\|_{\rm op}\le r_k^{-1}$. It follows from $K_N=C_NH_k^TS_N^{-1}$ and step 3.1 that $\sup_N\mathbb E\|K_N\|_{\rm op}^p<\infty$ at every finite order.

Let $D_i=y_k+\eta_{N,i}^k$. The update in [F1] gives $\|X_{N,i}^{a,k}\|\le\|X_{N,i}^{f,k}\|+\|K_N\|_{\rm op}\|H_kX_{N,i}^{f,k}\|+\|K_N\|_{\rm op}\|D_i\|$. Apply [F5] with exponent pair $(2,2)$ to the middle product; for the last product use that $D_i$ is independent of $K_N$ and has finite Gaussian moments. The forecast, gain, and perturbation bounds in steps 2.1 and 4.1 therefore bound the $p$th moment of the updated state uniformly in $N,i$. This proves the induction step at time $k$.

Step 1.1 proves the state bound at time zero. For each $k\in\{1,\ldots,T\}$, step 5.1 derives both the state and gain bounds at time $k$ from the state bound at time $k-1$. Finite induction therefore proves the state bounds for every $0\le k\le T$ and the gain bounds for every $1\le k\le T$, for each finite $p$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by

For integers $d,p\ge1$, given a forecast mean $m^f\in\mathbb R^d$, fixed background covariance $B\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, linear observation matrix $H\in\mathbb R^{p\times d}$, datum $y\in\mathbb R^p$, and observation-error covariance $\Gamma\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, require $B$ and $\Gamma$ symmetric positive definite. Define the 3DVAR objective
$$J(u)=\tfrac12(u-m^f)^TB^{-1}(u-m^f)+\tfrac12(y-Hu)^T\Gamma^{-1}(y-Hu).$$
Form $S=HBH^T+\Gamma$. It is positive definite because for every $z\ne0$,
$$z^TSz=(H^Tz)^TB(H^Tz)+z^T\Gamma z>0.$$
Factor $S=LL^T$ with the unique positive-diagonal Cholesky factor from [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]]. Solve $LW=HB$ and $L^TK^T=W$; thus $K^T=S^{-1}HB$ without explicitly forming $S^{-1}$. Return the analysis point
$$m^a=m^f+K(y-Hm^f).$$
For a sequential 3DVAR filter, first set $m^f_{j+1}=\Psi_j(m^a_j)$, then apply this update with the fixed matrices $B,H,\Gamma$ and observation $y_{j+1}$. The routine returns a point estimate only. Its unique-minimizer and Gaussian-MAP properties are established separately; no analysis covariance is returned.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional inner product spaces and let $b\in W$. A vector $x\in V$ minimises $\lVert Tx-b\rVert$ if and only if

$$T^*(Tx-b)=0,$$

equivalently $T^*Tx=T^*b$. Minimisers exist, and if $x_0$ is one minimiser, then the full set of minimisers is $x_0+\ker T$.

Let $n\ge 1$ and let $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$, with the real case obtained by
restricting scalars to $\mathbb R$. Then the following are equivalent:

1. $A$ has a Cholesky factorisation $A=LL^*$ with $L$ lower triangular and
   positive real diagonal.
2. $A$ is Hermitian positive definite.

When these conditions hold, the factor $L$ is unique.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $\Sigma$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. If $X\sim N_d(m,\Sigma)$, then its law has Lebesgue density
$$f_{m,\Sigma}(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma)^{-1/2} \exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(x-m)^T\Sigma^{-1}(x-m)\right), \qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.$$

Let $\pi$ be a prior probability on $(E,\mathcal S)$ and let $Q:E\to T$ be a probability kernel dominated by a sigma-finite measure $\nu$ on $(T,\mathcal T)$, with specified nonnegative jointly measurable density $\ell:E\times T\to[0,\infty]$:
$$Q(\theta,B)=\int_B\ell(\theta,y)\,\nu(dy)\quad\text{for every }\theta\in E,\ B\in\mathcal T.$$

Define $m(y)=\int_E\ell(\theta,y)\,\pi(d\theta)$. Under the joint law with density $\ell$ relative to $\pi\times\nu$, a conditional law of the parameter given the observation is
$$K(y,A)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{\int_A\ell(\theta,y)\,\pi(d\theta)}{m(y)},&0<m(y)<\infty,\\ \pi(A),&m(y)=0\text{ or }m(y)=\infty.\end{cases}$$

The observation marginal is $m\,d\nu$, and the filled fibres have marginal mass zero. This is a choice-free assertion about the explicit kernel and event identities.

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_0,\ldots,d_T$,
and positive observation dimensions $p_1,\ldots,p_T$. The input is a
linear-Gaussian model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]], with
matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_{k-1}}$ and
$H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, initial mean $m_0$, and symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariances $P_0,Q_k,R_k$. Its state and observation
equations are
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k,$$
where $q_k\sim N(0,Q_k)$ and $r_k\sim N(0,R_k)$ are centered and mutually
independent across all times and of $X_0$.

The admissible data are vectors $y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$ for which every
innovation covariance encountered below is positive definite. Positive
definite means $u^TS_ku>0$ for every nonzero $u\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$. The
algorithm returns predicted and updated means and covariances and the
innovation and gain at each time. Initialize
$$m_{0|0}=m_0,\qquad P_{0|0}=P_0.$$
For $k=1,\ldots,T$, perform:

1. Predict:
$$m_{k|k-1}=F_km_{k-1|k-1},\qquad P_{k|k-1}=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k.$$
2. Form the innovation and its covariance:
$$v_k=y_k-H_km_{k|k-1},\qquad S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k.$$
3. Factor $S_k=L_kL_k^T$ with lower-triangular $L_k$ having positive
diagonal, using
[[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]].
Solve $L_kU_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}$ and $L_k^TK_k^T=U_k$ by triangular solves. This
defines $K_k^T=S_k^{-1}H_kP_{k|k-1}$, hence
$K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS_k^{-1}$, without explicitly forming $S_k^{-1}$.
4. Update:
$$m_{k|k}=m_{k|k-1}+K_kv_k,\qquad P_{k|k}=P_{k|k-1}-K_kS_kK_k^T.$$

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the returned pair is $(m_0,P_0)$. No
inverse of $P_0$, $Q_k$, or $R_k$ is used. This item defines the procedure
and makes no complexity, rounding-error, or numerical-stability claim.

Assume AC. Fix a finite-horizon model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]] with
state and observation equations
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k\qquad (1\le k\le T),$$
where $X_0\sim N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$, the centered Gaussian noises $q_k,r_k$ are
mutually independent across times and from $X_0$, and $P_0,Q_k,R_k$ are
symmetric positive semidefinite. Let the parameters and observations be
admissible for [[alg-kalman-filter]], so the recursively formed innovation
covariances
$$S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k$$
are positive definite for every $1\le k\le T$. Run that algorithm from
$m_{0|0}=m_0$ and $P_{0|0}=P_0$. Then, for each $0\le k\le T$, the map
$$\pi_k(y_{1:k},\cdot)=N_{d_k}(m_{k|k}(y_{1:k}),P_{k|k})$$
is an everywhere-defined filtering kernel for $X_k$ given $Y_{1:k}$ in the
sense of [[def-state-space-filtering-laws]]. The empty history at $k=0$ is a
singleton, and $\pi_0=N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$. In particular, these recursions
give an exact Gaussian conditional-law version at every observation history;
each $P_{k|k}$ is positive semidefinite. Singular initial, process,
measurement, predicted-state, and filtered-state covariances are allowed.
Equivalently, the covariance update can be written in Joseph form
$$P_{k|k}=(I-K_kH_k)P_{k|k-1}(I-K_kH_k)^T+K_kR_kK_k^T.$$
Only the innovation matrices being solved must be positive definite. No
pointwise uniqueness of a conditional-law version on null histories,
observation-density assumption, or numerical-stability claim is made.

derivations.claim: For $z\ne0$, $z^TSz=(H^Tz)^TB(H^Tz)+z^T\Gamma z>0$, so $S\succ0$ and $K$ is defined. The inverses $B^{-1}$ and $\Gamma^{-1}$ are positive definite: for nonzero $v$, $v^TB^{-1}v=(B^{-1}v)^TB(B^{-1}v)>0$, and the same argument applies to $\Gamma$. By [F3], choose Cholesky factors $B^{-1}=L_BL_B^T$ and $\Gamma^{-1}=L_\Gamma L_\Gamma^T$. Define $T u=(L_B^Tu,L_\Gamma^THu)$ and $b=(L_B^Tm^f,L_\Gamma^Ty)$. Then $2J(u)=\|Tu-b\|^2$. The first block $L_B^T$ is invertible, hence $\ker T=\{0\}$.

The normal equation in [F2] is $B^{-1}(u-m^f)+H^T\Gamma^{-1}(Hu-y)=0$. Let $\delta=y-Hm^f$ and $u=m^f+BH^TS^{-1}\delta=m^a$. Then $B^{-1}(u-m^f)=H^TS^{-1}\delta$, while $y-Hu=(I-HBH^TS^{-1})\delta=\Gamma S^{-1}\delta$. Substitution gives the normal equation. By [F2] this $u$ minimizes $J$, and because $\ker T=\{0\}$ it is the unique minimizer.

Under the Gaussian prior and independent Gaussian observation-error model, [F4] gives a prior density proportional to $\exp[-\tfrac12(u-m^f)^TB^{-1}(u-m^f)]$ and a jointly continuous likelihood density proportional to $\exp[-\tfrac12(y-Hu)^T\Gamma^{-1}(y-Hu)]$. The likelihood is strictly positive and bounded above by its finite Gaussian normalizing constant; hence its prior integral is finite and positive. Bayes' formula [F5] makes the posterior density proportional to $e^{-J(u)}$; its unique maximum is therefore the unique minimizer from step 2.1.

Apply [F6] to the one-step model with forecast covariance $B$, identity transition, zero process covariance, and observation covariance $\Gamma$. Its innovation covariance is $S\succ0$ by step 1.1, so the output mean is $m^f+K(y-Hm^f)=m^a$. By [F7] this is the mean of the exact conditional Gaussian law.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$. Let
the state dimension at time
$t$ be a positive integer $d_t$ for $0\le t\le T$, and the observation
dimension at time $t$ be a positive integer $p_t$ for $1\le t\le T$.
Choose deterministic matrices
$F_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_{t-1}}$ and
$H_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t\times d_t}$, a mean $m_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$, and
symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices, meaning $v^TPv\ge0$ for every
real vector $v$ of matching dimension,
$P_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times d_0}$,
$Q_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_t}$, and
$R_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t\times p_t}$. A **linear-Gaussian state-space model
with independent noises** is the general finite-horizon kernel model
([[def-general-state-space-model-by-kernels]]) with initial law
$\mu_0=N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$ and transition and observation kernels
$$K_t(x,\cdot)=N_{d_t}(F_t x,Q_t),\qquad G_t(x,\cdot)=N_{p_t}(H_t x,R_t).$$
All Gaussian laws use the convention of
[[def-multivariate-normal-law]], which allows singular covariance matrices.

Its independent-noise representation consists of random vectors
$x_0,q_1,r_1,\ldots,q_T,r_T$ on a common probability space, with
$x_0\sim N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$, $q_t\sim N_{d_t}(0,Q_t)$,
$r_t\sim N_{p_t}(0,R_t)$, all mutually independent in the sense of
[[def-independent-random-elements]] (their generated sigma-algebras are
independent), and equations
$$x_t=F_t x_{t-1}+q_t,\qquad y_t=H_t x_t+r_t\qquad(1\le t\le T).$$
The local path-law theorem proves that every allowed parameter tuple has
such a finite representation, that its induced kernels are the displayed
$K_t,G_t$, and that its path law is the general kernel-product law.

This definition imposes the stated noise law and independence assumptions;
it does not establish their empirical adequacy. It supplies no filtering
algorithm, posterior recursion, or convergence claim. Any separate formula
that inverts an observed innovation covariance must assume that covariance is
positive definite at the point of inversion.

Fix an ensemble size $N\ge2$, forecast map $\Psi$, observation map $G$, datum $y\in\mathbb R^p$, and observation covariance $\Gamma\succ0$. The input is a state ensemble $x^1,\ldots,x^N\in\mathbb R^d$, forecast-error draws $\xi^i$ that are independent across members and of the input ensemble, each with the caller-specified additive model-error law, and observation perturbations $\eta^i\sim N_p(0,\Gamma)$ under [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]. The observation perturbations are independent across members and independent of the forecast ensemble and forecast-error draws.

1. Forecast each member: $\widehat x^i=\Psi(x^i)+\xi^i$.

2. Form predicted observations $z^i=G(\widehat x^i)$, means $\bar x=N^{-1}\sum_i\widehat x^i$, $\bar z=N^{-1}\sum_i z^i$, and empirical covariance blocks
$$C_{xz}=N^{-1}\sum_i(\widehat x^i-\bar x)(z^i-\bar z)^T,\qquad C_{zz}=N^{-1}\sum_i(z^i-\bar z)(z^i-\bar z)^T.$$
The divisor-$N$ convention is part of this algorithm.

3. Form $S_N=C_{zz}+\Gamma$. Since $C_{zz}$ is positive semidefinite and $\Gamma$ is positive definite, $S_N$ is positive definite. Factor it by Cholesky and solve $S_NK_N^T=C_{xz}^T$ by triangular solves.

4. Update every member using its perturbed datum:
$$x^{a,i}=\widehat x^i+K_N(y+\eta^i-z^i).$$

Return the updated ensemble and its empirical mean and covariance. When $G(x)=Hx$, $C_{xz}=C_xH^T$ and $C_{zz}=HC_xH^T$, giving the usual sample-covariance Kalman gain. This item specifies the perturbed-observation variant; deterministic square-root updates are different finite-ensemble procedures. Finite ensembles in nonlinear models are approximations and carry no general posterior-exactness claim.

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_0,\ldots,d_T$,
and positive observation dimensions $p_1,\ldots,p_T$. The input is a
linear-Gaussian model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]], with
matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_{k-1}}$ and
$H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, initial mean $m_0$, and symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariances $P_0,Q_k,R_k$. Its state and observation
equations are
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k,$$
where $q_k\sim N(0,Q_k)$ and $r_k\sim N(0,R_k)$ are centered and mutually
independent across all times and of $X_0$.

The admissible data are vectors $y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$ for which every
innovation covariance encountered below is positive definite. Positive
definite means $u^TS_ku>0$ for every nonzero $u\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$. The
algorithm returns predicted and updated means and covariances and the
innovation and gain at each time. Initialize
$$m_{0|0}=m_0,\qquad P_{0|0}=P_0.$$
For $k=1,\ldots,T$, perform:

1. Predict:
$$m_{k|k-1}=F_km_{k-1|k-1},\qquad P_{k|k-1}=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k.$$
2. Form the innovation and its covariance:
$$v_k=y_k-H_km_{k|k-1},\qquad S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k.$$
3. Factor $S_k=L_kL_k^T$ with lower-triangular $L_k$ having positive
diagonal, using
[[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]].
Solve $L_kU_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}$ and $L_k^TK_k^T=U_k$ by triangular solves. This
defines $K_k^T=S_k^{-1}H_kP_{k|k-1}$, hence
$K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS_k^{-1}$, without explicitly forming $S_k^{-1}$.
4. Update:
$$m_{k|k}=m_{k|k-1}+K_kv_k,\qquad P_{k|k}=P_{k|k-1}-K_kS_kK_k^T.$$

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the returned pair is $(m_0,P_0)$. No
inverse of $P_0$, $Q_k$, or $R_k$ is used. This item defines the procedure
and makes no complexity, rounding-error, or numerical-stability claim.

Assume AC. Fix a finite-horizon model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]] with
state and observation equations
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k\qquad (1\le k\le T),$$
where $X_0\sim N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$, the centered Gaussian noises $q_k,r_k$ are
mutually independent across times and from $X_0$, and $P_0,Q_k,R_k$ are
symmetric positive semidefinite. Let the parameters and observations be
admissible for [[alg-kalman-filter]], so the recursively formed innovation
covariances
$$S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k$$
are positive definite for every $1\le k\le T$. Run that algorithm from
$m_{0|0}=m_0$ and $P_{0|0}=P_0$. Then, for each $0\le k\le T$, the map
$$\pi_k(y_{1:k},\cdot)=N_{d_k}(m_{k|k}(y_{1:k}),P_{k|k})$$
is an everywhere-defined filtering kernel for $X_k$ given $Y_{1:k}$ in the
sense of [[def-state-space-filtering-laws]]. The empty history at $k=0$ is a
singleton, and $\pi_0=N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$. In particular, these recursions
give an exact Gaussian conditional-law version at every observation history;
each $P_{k|k}$ is positive semidefinite. Singular initial, process,
measurement, predicted-state, and filtered-state covariances are allowed.
Equivalently, the covariance update can be written in Joseph form
$$P_{k|k}=(I-K_kH_k)P_{k|k-1}(I-K_kH_k)^T+K_kR_kK_k^T.$$
Only the innovation matrices being solved must be positive definite. No
pointwise uniqueness of a conditional-law version on null histories,
observation-density assumption, or numerical-stability claim is made.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space and let $T:V\to V$ be
self-adjoint. Then $V$ has an orthonormal basis consisting of eigenvectors of
$T$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $X_0,\dots,X_{n-1}$ be independent real random variables on a
common probability space, and let $g_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be Borel
measurable for each $i<n$.

1. If every $g_i$ is nonnegative, then
   $$\mathbb E\left[\prod_{i<n}g_i(X_i)\right]=\prod_{i<n}\mathbb E[g_i(X_i)]$$
   in $[0,+\infty]$. In this finite product of expectations, a zero factor
   makes the product zero even when another factor is $+\infty$; otherwise
   multiplication has its usual extended nonnegative meaning.
2. If every $g_i(X_i)$ is integrable, then $\prod_{i<n}g_i(X_i)$ is integrable
   and the same factorization holds in $\mathbb R$.

Let $f:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable and let $t>0$. Then
$$\mu(\{f\ge t\})\le\frac1t\int f\,d\mu.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $m\ge1$ be finite, let $d_j\ge1$, and let
$Z_j$ for $1\le j\le m$ be mutually independent random elements of
$\mathbb R^{d_j}$. Suppose $Z_j\sim N_{d_j}(a_j,\Sigma_j)$, where each
$\Sigma_j$ is symmetric positive semidefinite. Put
$D=\sum_{j=1}^m d_j$, $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m)$,
$a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$, and
$\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_m)$. Then
$$Z\sim N_D(a,\Sigma).$$
No covariance block needs to be invertible.

Fix the perturbed-observation update of [[alg-ensemble-kalman-filter]]. A row of random inputs is **exchangeable** if its joint law is invariant under every common permutation of the member indices. If the forecast states, forecast errors, observation perturbations, and any reference-member variables form an exchangeable input row, then the updated states together with those reference variables are exchangeable.

Let $d\ge1$. For each $N\ge2$, let $(X_{N,i},U_{N,i})_{i=1}^N$ be jointly exchangeable random pairs in $\mathbb R^d$. Assume that $U_{N,1},\ldots,U_{N,N}$ are iid with the law of a fixed $U$, $\mathbb E\|U\|^4<\infty$, and $\|X_{N,1}-U_{N,1}\|_4\to0$. Define
$$\bar X_N=N^{-1}\sum_iX_{N,i},\qquad C_N=N^{-1}\sum_i(X_{N,i}-\bar X_N)(X_{N,i}-\bar X_N)^T.$$
Here $\operatorname{Cov}(U):=\mathbb E[(U-\mathbb EU)(U-\mathbb EU)^T]$. Then $\bar X_N\to\mathbb EU$ and $C_N\to\operatorname{Cov}(U)$ in probability, entry by entry.

Assume AC and the finite-horizon linear-Gaussian model of [[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]], with $R_k\succ0$ for $1\le k\le T$. Fix the observation values $y_{1:T}$. For each $N$, initialize $U_{N,i}^{a,0}$ iid with the model's $N(m_0,P_0)$ prior. At each time use independent per-member noises $q_{N,i}^k\sim N(0,Q_k)$ and $\eta_{N,i}^k\sim N(0,R_k)$, independent across $i,k$ and from the preceding ensemble, and form
$$U_{N,i}^{f,k}=F_kU_{N,i}^{a,k-1}+q_{N,i}^k,\qquad U_{N,i}^{a,k}=U_{N,i}^{f,k}+K_k(y_k+\eta_{N,i}^k-H_kU_{N,i}^{f,k}),$$
where $K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^T(H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k)^{-1}$ is the deterministic gain from [[alg-kalman-filter]]. Then, for every $k\le T$, the analysis members $U_{N,1}^{a,k},\ldots,U_{N,N}^{a,k}$ are iid with law $N(m_{k|k},P_{k|k})$, the exact Kalman filtering law at the fixed data $y_{1:k}$.

Fix a finite horizon linear-Gaussian model from [[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]], with each observation covariance $R_k\succ0$. Run the perturbed-observation procedure of [[alg-ensemble-kalman-filter]] with iid Gaussian initial members and independent Gaussian process and observation perturbations having the model's laws. For every finite $p\ge1$, there are constants $c_{k,p}$ for $0\le k\le T$ and $b_{k,p}$ for $1\le k\le T$, independent of ensemble size $N\ge2$ and member index $i$, such that
$$\sup_{N,i}\mathbb E\|X_{N,i}^{a,k}\|^p\le c_{k,p}\quad(0\le k\le T),\qquad \sup_N\mathbb E\|K_N^k\|_{\rm op}^p\le b_{k,p}\quad(1\le k\le T).$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_{\rm op}$ is the Euclidean operator norm. The claim is for each fixed finite horizon, not a bound uniform in $k$ as the horizon grows.

Let $1\le q<s<\infty$. Suppose random vectors $Z_n,Z$ in a fixed finite-dimensional Euclidean space satisfy $Z_n\to Z$ in probability, $\mathbb E\|Z\|^s<\infty$, and $\sup_n\mathbb E\|Z_n\|^s<\infty$. Then $\mathbb E\|Z_n-Z\|^q\to0$.

derivations.claim: Couple the EnKF members with a reference ensemble by using the same iid initial vectors, process-error draws, and perturbed observations. At time $0$, $X_{N,i}^{a,0}=U_{N,i}^{a,0}$, so the paired row is exchangeable and the memberwise difference is zero in every finite $L^p$.

Fix $k\in\{1,\ldots,T\}$ and assume the induction hypothesis: the paired analysis row $(X_{N,i}^{a,k-1},U_{N,i}^{a,k-1})_{i=1}^N$ is exchangeable and $\|X_{N,1}^{a,k-1}-U_{N,1}^{a,k-1}\|_p\to0$ for every finite $p$. Couple the forecasts with the same $q_{N,i}^k$; then $X_{N,i}^{f,k}-U_{N,i}^{f,k}=F_k(X_{N,i}^{a,k-1}-U_{N,i}^{a,k-1})$. Thus forecast differences tend to zero in every finite $L^p$. The independent iid process-error and observation-perturbation rows have permutation-invariant laws and are independent of the paired analysis row; their product with that row is permutation-invariant, and the same forecast map is applied to each member. Hence the forecast pair row with its perturbations is exchangeable. By [F8] and [F1], each reference forecast is Gaussian, with mean and covariance $m^f=F_km_{k-1|k-1}$ and $P^f=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k$ as in [F3]; independence across members follows from the independent per-member inputs.

Apply [L2] to the forecast pair row with $p=4$. The reference forecast covariance is $P_{k|k-1}$ by [F1] and [F3], so $C_N^{f,k}\to P_{k|k-1}$ in probability. Since $R_k\succ0$, both $S_N=H_kC_N^{f,k}H_k^T+R_k$ and $S=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k$ dominate $R_k$ in quadratic form. [F5] bounds both inverse operator norms by $1/\lambda_{\min}(R_k)$. The identity $S_N^{-1}-S^{-1}=S_N^{-1}(S-S_N)S^{-1}$ therefore gives $K_N^k=C_N^{f,k}H_k^TS_N^{-1}\to K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS^{-1}$ in probability.

Let $D_{N,i}^k=y_k+\eta_{N,i}^k$. Subtracting the reference update from the EnKF update yields $X_{N,i}^{a,k}-U_{N,i}^{a,k}=(I-K_N^kH_k)(X_{N,i}^{f,k}-U_{N,i}^{f,k})+(K_N^k-K_k)(D_{N,i}^k-H_kU_{N,i}^{f,k}).$ The first factor in the first product is bounded in probability because $K_N^k\to K_k$ in probability. The first factor in the second product tends to zero in probability, while $D_{N,i}^k-H_kU_{N,i}^{f,k}$ has a fixed finite-moment Gaussian law. Splitting on whether this latter norm exceeds an arbitrary $M$ shows the product tends to zero in probability. The same bounded-in-probability argument for the first product gives $X_{N,1}^{a,k}-U_{N,1}^{a,k}\to0$ in probability. By [L1], the updated paired row is exchangeable.

The uniform moment bounds [L4] and the Gaussian reference law [L3] give a uniform bound on $\mathbb E\|X_{N,1}^{a,k}-U_{N,1}^{a,k}\|^s$ for every finite $s$. Apply [L5] with any $s>p$ to the probability convergence in step 4.1; the memberwise difference tends to zero in $L^p$ for every finite $p$. Together, the preceding steps establish the induction hypothesis at time $k$.

At any fixed $k$, the paired row is exchangeable, the reference members are iid with law $\pi_k$ by [L3], and [F4] identifies that Kalman law with the exact filtering law at the fixed data. At $k=0$, the memberwise difference is identically zero by step 1.1, hence tends to zero in $L^4$; for $k\ge1$, it tends to zero in $L^4$ by step 5.1. The sample-moment result [L2] gives the claimed mean and covariance convergence. For bounded Lipschitz $\varphi$, the empirical-average difference is at most $\operatorname{Lip}(\varphi)N^{-1}\sum_i\|X_{N,i}^{a,k}-U_{N,i}^{a,k}\|$; its expectation tends to zero by exchangeability and the $L^1$ convergence in step 1.1 when $k=0$ and step 5.1 when $k\ge1$, so the pointwise bound $\mathbb P(W\ge t)\le t^{-1}\mathbb EW$ from [F7] makes it vanish in probability. For the iid reference average, independence [F6] makes all distinct centered cross terms have expectation zero, so its variance is $\operatorname{Var}(\varphi(U_{N,1}^{a,k}))/N\le\|\varphi\|_\infty^2/N$. Apply [F7] to its squared centered deviation at threshold $\epsilon^2$ to obtain convergence in probability to $\int\varphi\,d\pi_k$. This proves the limits for each fixed $k$.

Step 1.1 is the base case, and for every $k\ge1$ the four induction steps establish the induction hypothesis at time $k$ from time $k-1$. Thus the coupling bounds hold through $T$, and step 6.1 gives the three asserted limits for every fixed $k\le T$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

Assume AC and let $d\ge1$ be finite. For $m\in\mathbb R^d$ and a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix $\Sigma$, a Borel probability law is denoted $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ when a vector X with that law satisfies $u\cdot X\sim N(u\cdot m,u^T\Sigma u)$ for every $u\in\mathbb R^d$. Such a law exists, has mean m and covariance Sigma, and can be realized as $m+\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ with independent standard-normal coordinates. Singular Sigma is allowed. Uniqueness will be proved in the following characteristic-function lemma.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $\Sigma$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. If $X\sim N_d(m,\Sigma)$, then its law has Lebesgue density
$$f_{m,\Sigma}(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma)^{-1/2} \exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(x-m)^T\Sigma^{-1}(x-m)\right), \qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.$$

Let $\pi$ be a prior probability on $(E,\mathcal S)$ and let $Q:E\to T$ be a probability kernel dominated by a sigma-finite measure $\nu$ on $(T,\mathcal T)$, with specified nonnegative jointly measurable density $\ell:E\times T\to[0,\infty]$:
$$Q(\theta,B)=\int_B\ell(\theta,y)\,\nu(dy)\quad\text{for every }\theta\in E,\ B\in\mathcal T.$$

Define $m(y)=\int_E\ell(\theta,y)\,\pi(d\theta)$. Under the joint law with density $\ell$ relative to $\pi\times\nu$, a conditional law of the parameter given the observation is
$$K(y,A)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{\int_A\ell(\theta,y)\,\pi(d\theta)}{m(y)},&0<m(y)<\infty,\\ \pi(A),&m(y)=0\text{ or }m(y)=\infty.\end{cases}$$

The observation marginal is $m\,d\nu$, and the filled fibres have marginal mass zero. This is a choice-free assertion about the explicit kernel and event identities.

Fix an ensemble size $N\ge2$, forecast map $\Psi$, observation map $G$, datum $y\in\mathbb R^p$, and observation covariance $\Gamma\succ0$. The input is a state ensemble $x^1,\ldots,x^N\in\mathbb R^d$, forecast-error draws $\xi^i$ that are independent across members and of the input ensemble, each with the caller-specified additive model-error law, and observation perturbations $\eta^i\sim N_p(0,\Gamma)$ under [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]. The observation perturbations are independent across members and independent of the forecast ensemble and forecast-error draws.

1. Forecast each member: $\widehat x^i=\Psi(x^i)+\xi^i$.

2. Form predicted observations $z^i=G(\widehat x^i)$, means $\bar x=N^{-1}\sum_i\widehat x^i$, $\bar z=N^{-1}\sum_i z^i$, and empirical covariance blocks
$$C_{xz}=N^{-1}\sum_i(\widehat x^i-\bar x)(z^i-\bar z)^T,\qquad C_{zz}=N^{-1}\sum_i(z^i-\bar z)(z^i-\bar z)^T.$$
The divisor-$N$ convention is part of this algorithm.

3. Form $S_N=C_{zz}+\Gamma$. Since $C_{zz}$ is positive semidefinite and $\Gamma$ is positive definite, $S_N$ is positive definite. Factor it by Cholesky and solve $S_NK_N^T=C_{xz}^T$ by triangular solves.

4. Update every member using its perturbed datum:
$$x^{a,i}=\widehat x^i+K_N(y+\eta^i-z^i).$$

Return the updated ensemble and its empirical mean and covariance. When $G(x)=Hx$, $C_{xz}=C_xH^T$ and $C_{zz}=HC_xH^T$, giving the usual sample-covariance Kalman gain. derivations.claim: The predicted observations of both ensemble members equal $1$, so their empirical observation variance is $0$. Their empirical state-observation cross-covariance is also $0$, because the observation deviations are both zero. By [F5] and $\gamma>0$, the gain is zero; the update is therefore $x^{a,1}=-1$, $x^{a,2}=1$ for every perturbation realization. The updated empirical variance remains $1$.

By [A1], [F1], and [F3], the prior and Gaussian likelihood have densities. The likelihood is positive and bounded, so its prior integral is finite and positive; Bayes' formula [F4] makes the posterior density proportional to the even function $e^{-x^2/2}w(x^2)$, where $w(t)=e^{-t^2/(2\gamma)}$. The posterior mean is therefore zero by symmetry. Put $T=X^2$. Since $\mathbb ET=1$ by [F2], $\mathbb E[(T-1)w(T)]=\mathbb E[(T-1)(w(T)-w(1))]<0.$ The equality uses $\mathbb E(T-1)=0$. The inequality holds because $w$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,\infty)$, so the integrand is negative whenever $T\ne1$; the standard normal density gives $\mathbb P(T=1)=0$. The integrand is integrable since $0<w\le1$ and $\mathbb ET<\infty$. Thus the posterior variance is $\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y=0)=\frac{\mathbb E[T w(T)]}{\mathbb E[w(T)]}<1.$ The finite EnKF ensemble variance from step 1.1 is $1$, so this admissible nonlinear finite-ensemble update does not equal the exact posterior law.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$. Let
the state dimension at time
$t$ be a positive integer $d_t$ for $0\le t\le T$, and the observation
dimension at time $t$ be a positive integer $p_t$ for $1\le t\le T$.
Choose deterministic matrices
$F_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_{t-1}}$ and
$H_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t\times d_t}$, a mean $m_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$, and
symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices, meaning $v^TPv\ge0$ for every
real vector $v$ of matching dimension,
$P_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times d_0}$,
$Q_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_t}$, and
$R_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t\times p_t}$. A **linear-Gaussian state-space model
with independent noises** is the general finite-horizon kernel model
([[def-general-state-space-model-by-kernels]]) with initial law
$\mu_0=N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$ and transition and observation kernels
$$K_t(x,\cdot)=N_{d_t}(F_t x,Q_t),\qquad G_t(x,\cdot)=N_{p_t}(H_t x,R_t).$$
All Gaussian laws use the convention of
[[def-multivariate-normal-law]], which allows singular covariance matrices.

Its independent-noise representation consists of random vectors
$x_0,q_1,r_1,\ldots,q_T,r_T$ on a common probability space, with
$x_0\sim N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$, $q_t\sim N_{d_t}(0,Q_t)$,
$r_t\sim N_{p_t}(0,R_t)$, all mutually independent in the sense of
[[def-independent-random-elements]] (their generated sigma-algebras are
independent), and equations
$$x_t=F_t x_{t-1}+q_t,\qquad y_t=H_t x_t+r_t\qquad(1\le t\le T).$$
The local path-law theorem proves that every allowed parameter tuple has
such a finite representation, that its induced kernels are the displayed
$K_t,G_t$, and that its path law is the general kernel-product law.

This definition imposes the stated noise law and independence assumptions;
it does not establish their empirical adequacy. It supplies no filtering
algorithm, posterior recursion, or convergence claim. Any separate formula
that inverts an observed innovation covariance must assume that covariance is
positive definite at the point of inversion.

For integers $d,p\ge1$, given a forecast mean $m^f\in\mathbb R^d$, fixed background covariance $B\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, linear observation matrix $H\in\mathbb R^{p\times d}$, datum $y\in\mathbb R^p$, and observation-error covariance $\Gamma\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, require $B$ and $\Gamma$ symmetric positive definite. Define the 3DVAR objective
$$J(u)=\tfrac12(u-m^f)^TB^{-1}(u-m^f)+\tfrac12(y-Hu)^T\Gamma^{-1}(y-Hu).$$
Form $S=HBH^T+\Gamma$. It is positive definite because for every $z\ne0$,
$$z^TSz=(H^Tz)^TB(H^Tz)+z^T\Gamma z>0.$$
Factor $S=LL^T$ with the unique positive-diagonal Cholesky factor from [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]]. Solve $LW=HB$ and $L^TK^T=W$; thus $K^T=S^{-1}HB$ without explicitly forming $S^{-1}$. Return the analysis point
$$m^a=m^f+K(y-Hm^f).$$
For a sequential 3DVAR filter, first set $m^f_{j+1}=\Psi_j(m^a_j)$, then apply this update with the fixed matrices $B,H,\Gamma$ and observation $y_{j+1}$. The routine returns a point estimate only. Its unique-minimizer and Gaussian-MAP properties are established separately; no analysis covariance is returned.

Let $d,p\ge1$, $m^f\in\mathbb R^d$, $y\in\mathbb R^p$, $H\in\mathbb R^{p\times d}$, and symmetric positive-definite $B\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ and $\Gamma\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$. Put $S=HBH^T+\Gamma$, $K=BH^TS^{-1}$, and
$$J(u)=\tfrac12(u-m^f)^TB^{-1}(u-m^f)+\tfrac12(y-Hu)^T\Gamma^{-1}(y-Hu).$$
The 3DVAR analysis $m^a=m^f+K(y-Hm^f)$ from [[alg-three-dimensional-variational-assimilation]] is the unique global minimizer of $J$. If $m^f,B$ are the mean and covariance of a Gaussian forecast and the observation model is $Y=HX+r$ with independent $r\sim N_p(0,\Gamma)$, then $m^a$ is the unique maximum-a-posteriori point of the posterior density. It is also the mean update of the exact one-step Kalman filter with identity state transition, zero process covariance, and datum $y$.

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_0,\ldots,d_T$,
and positive observation dimensions $p_1,\ldots,p_T$. The input is a
linear-Gaussian model from
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]], with
matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_{k-1}}$ and
$H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, initial mean $m_0$, and symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariances $P_0,Q_k,R_k$. Its state and observation
equations are
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k,$$
where $q_k\sim N(0,Q_k)$ and $r_k\sim N(0,R_k)$ are centered and mutually
independent across all times and of $X_0$.

The admissible data are vectors $y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$ for which every
innovation covariance encountered below is positive definite. Positive
definite means $u^TS_ku>0$ for every nonzero $u\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$. The
algorithm returns predicted and updated means and covariances and the
innovation and gain at each time. Initialize
$$m_{0|0}=m_0,\qquad P_{0|0}=P_0.$$
For $k=1,\ldots,T$, perform:

1. Predict:
$$m_{k|k-1}=F_km_{k-1|k-1},\qquad P_{k|k-1}=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k.$$
2. Form the innovation and its covariance:
$$v_k=y_k-H_km_{k|k-1},\qquad S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k.$$
3. Factor $S_k=L_kL_k^T$ with lower-triangular $L_k$ having positive
diagonal, using
[[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]].
Solve $L_kU_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}$ and $L_k^TK_k^T=U_k$ by triangular solves. This
defines $K_k^T=S_k^{-1}H_kP_{k|k-1}$, hence
$K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS_k^{-1}$, without explicitly forming $S_k^{-1}$.
4. Update:
$$m_{k|k}=m_{k|k-1}+K_kv_k,\qquad P_{k|k}=P_{k|k-1}-K_kS_kK_k^T.$$

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the returned pair is $(m_0,P_0)$. No
inverse of $P_0$, $Q_k$, or $R_k$ is used. This item defines the procedure
and makes no complexity, rounding-error, or numerical-stability claim.

state and observation equations
$$X_k=F_kX_{k-1}+q_k,\qquad Y_k=H_kX_k+r_k\qquad (1\le k\le T),$$
where $X_0\sim N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$, the centered Gaussian noises $q_k,r_k$ are

admissible for [[alg-kalman-filter]], so the recursively formed innovation
covariances
$$S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k$$

$$\pi_k(y_{1:k},\cdot)=N_{d_k}(m_{k|k}(y_{1:k}),P_{k|k})$$
is an everywhere-defined filtering kernel for $X_k$ given $Y_{1:k}$ in the
sense of [[def-state-space-filtering-laws]]. The empty history at $k=0$ is a
singleton, and $\pi_0=N_{d_0}(m_0,P_0)$. In particular, these recursions
give an exact Gaussian conditional-law version at every observation history;
each $P_{k|k}$ is positive semidefinite. Singular initial, process,

$$P_{k|k}=(I-K_kH_k)P_{k|k-1}(I-K_kH_k)^T+K_kR_kK_k^T.$$

pointwise uniqueness of a conditional-law version on null histories,
observation-density assumption, or numerical-stability claim is made.
